item.description: - **Edit from here & deeper search:** Rewind any sent message in place (choosing to revert or keep files in isolated worktrees) and edit your prompt before resending. Search across full thread history (`⌘F`), including older unloaded turns, match branches, pull requests, and message text in sidebar search, and cite any assistant excerpt directly into the composer as a `@quote` chip. - **Sidebar triage & Command Palette:** Active runs that don’t need your input now fold into a collapsible **Working** shelf on Mac and iPhone so Active stays focused on what needs attention. Settle, snooze, unpin, and archive show a 5-second Undo toast (`⌘Z` on Mac), with multi-select bulk triage, custom snooze times, editable presets, and opt-in idle auto-settle with a per-thread *Never Auto-Settle* toggle. Press `⌘K` on Mac for the new Command Palette and `⌘1–⌘9` to jump straight to inbox threads. - **Composer upgrades & multi-model fan-out:** Edit queued prompts in place, promote any queued prompt with *Send Now*, reorder the queue, and pick your default Queue vs. Steer follow-up mode. Large pastes (≥ 32 KiB) attach automatically as files, `↑`/`↓` recalls earlier prompts, `⌘S` stashes drafts for later, `⌘⌥⏎` sends in the background and opens a fresh draft, and *Compare Models…* launches parallel isolated worktree threads across multiple models. - **Inspector tabs, Git review & automatic worktree cleanup:** The Mac Inspector now opens files, diffs, PRs, subagents, and browser pages as multi-instance tabs with *Close Others* and `⇧⌘T` reopen, plus scoped per-turn and per-tool diffs. Pull request review adds per-file *Viewed* tracking, Auto-Merge, Revert PR, optional AI credit stripping, clean default-branch auto-pull, and branch naming prefixes. Settings → Worktrees adds opt-in safe automatic worktree cleanup with an audit log. - **Schedules, CLI, deep links & Mac polish:** View, create, pause, run now, and delete recurring schedules and `/heartbeat` prompts from Settings → **Schedules** on Mac and iPhone. Install the `controller` CLI from Settings → General (`controller .`, `controller new`, `controller run --wait`) or open prefilled drafts via `controller://new?...` deep links. Mac also adds Launch at Login, a Dock attention badge, distinct completion and needs-input sound cues, and smarter onboarding discovery for harnesses, local Git repos, and past Claude/Codex sessions. - **iPhone widgets, Share Extension, multi-Mac & UI polish:** iPhone and iPad add Home and Lock Screen widgets for active agents and subscription usage, an iOS Share Extension for sending links, text, images, and files straight into Controller, *Auto (Least Busy Mac)* selection with live host headroom, loopback-safe remote dev server preview forwarding, refined iPhone Duo composer/model picker/task plan chip animations, and improved Antigravity 1.5.16 native edit diffs.

- You can now remove any non-built-in harness account even when it has existing conversations, native bindings, or project defaults. Idle conversations keep their history, switch to your fallback account, and hand off prior context automatically on the next turn; removal is only blocked while active work or pending requests are running on that account. - Fixed an error where Muse Code could show `Swift.CancellationError` after background discovery refreshed unchanged account settings while it was connecting. - Antigravity updates to Google's official Antigravity CLI 1.5.16 runtime with direct mid-turn steering (keeping running subagents and background tasks alive), native system prompt append, tool-free sessions, ACP form elicitation, and isolated file token storage. - Managed Pi accounts now use Pi 1.6.0, Cursor accounts now use Cursor SDK 1.5.0 (Settings offers the new downloads), Factory Droid SDK accounts now use `@factory/droid-sdk` 0.11.0, and Muse Code adds Muse 1.4.24 session-rename capability negotiation and described reasoning effort variants.

- Streamed replies on Mac, iPhone and iPad now glide in with spring-driven Metal animations, voice dictation morphs into the composer with a smoke transition and glowing waveform, and the reasoning effort slider renders animated sparkles and speed streaks on the GPU (all honoring Reduce Motion). - Antigravity updates to ACP 1.5.0 with compaction progress reporting and now supports running through your installed `agy` CLI. - Siri on Mac can now discover and interact with your local chats, and Siri on iPhone and iPad resolves projects by host Mac. - Long chats stay smoother while an agent is replying: Mac, iPhone and iPad reuse work on the active reply (including tables and file links), iPhone keeps offscreen rows out of memory, and Claude Code threads release finished messages sooner. - Broad reliability, memory and battery improvements across Mac, iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch reduce idle wakeups, redundant Git and Connect polling, and view leaks while keeping composer paste, page navigation, and repository browsing responsive. - The task plan pill grows to fit larger text sizes on Mac, iPhone and iPad, nearby composer cards make room for it, and on iPhone Settled, New Chat and expanded project rows stay reliably visible and tappable. - Controller Connect is more dependable and quieter in the background. A Mac no longer shows as reachable after its tunnel fails, an expired tunnel certificate is replaced instead of served, reconnecting downloads only what changed, returning to the app on iPhone or iPad no longer wakes a sleeping Mac, and an idle Mac makes fewer requests. A Mac with **Notify me about remote work** off can still relay a wake request at once. - Remote access is tighter. The local network shortcut accepts only private addresses and encrypted sessions, a pairing link asks before it saves a new Mac, memory sync runs only between your own Macs over encrypted sessions, and remote devices can no longer add the home folder or a folder holding credentials as a project. - Agents that run other agents stay within their own access. Scheduled threads inherit the limits of the thread that scheduled them, approving another thread's request needs the access to have run it yourself, and commit and pull request text is written without letting the model run tools. A thread no longer stays stuck sending after a harness fails to start, queued steering prompts are no longer lost, and approval cards expire instead of vanishing when a harness quits.
